# Troubleshooting quick reference

Error message / symptom → likely cause → fix.

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `404` on `GET /v1/workspaces/<id>` even though you're logged in | The workspace belongs to a different tenant than your current `az` login, or your account genuinely has no access to it | `az account show` to confirm the active identity/tenant; `az login` again as the correct account if needed. A 404 (not 403) here usually means "wrong tenant/no visibility", not "exists but forbidden" |
| List Paths call returns the Lakehouse's own top-level folders (`Files`, `Tables`, ...) instead of your target subfolder's contents | Workspace **and** item both put in the URL path, with the target path in `directory` — ADLS Gen2 List Paths expects only the workspace (filesystem) in the path | Put the item GUID as the *first segment* of `directory` instead: `.../<workspaceId>?resource=filesystem&directory=<itemId>/Files/...`. See [onelake-rest-api.md](onelake-rest-api.md) |
| `401`/`403` calling `api.fabric.microsoft.com` even though a token was fetched successfully | Token was requested for the wrong resource/audience (e.g. `https://storage.azure.com` instead of `https://api.fabric.microsoft.com`, or vice versa) | Re-request the token with the correct `--resource` for the API you're calling. See [auth-and-tokens.md](auth-and-tokens.md) |
| A specific column is 100% `NULL` in a CDC-mirrored current-state table, but the related columns look fine | "Keep latest row per PK" dedup without forward-fill — the column's only real value was set at an earlier event and got dropped when a later, unrelated update became "the latest row" | Apply the forward-fill fix in [cdc-mirroring-and-dedup.md](cdc-mirroring-and-dedup.md) and re-run |
| A whole set of expected columns is simply *missing* from the flattened output (not present at all, not even as null) | The source columns were binary/blob type and an explicit binary-handling step dropped them (common because most flat formats like CSV can't represent binary) | Check the transform's binary-column-drop logic/log; if the content is actually needed, switch it to base64-encode instead of drop |
| `az login` fails or nags about subscriptions in a Fabric-only trial tenant | No Azure subscription attached to that tenant — normal for Fabric-only trials | `az login --use-device-code --allow-no-subscriptions` |
| Uploading many files one-by-one to OneLake is slow / hits rate limits | No batch upload API — every file is its own create+append+flush sequence | Keep individual files small where possible (Delta writes many small Parquet parts by default in most cases); avoid uploading extremely large files in a single `append` call — chunk large files into multiple sequential append calls at increasing `position` offsets instead of one giant call |
| A very long inline shell command (e.g. a giant generated SQL statement passed as a single `-c` argument) fails with an OS-level "argument list too long" / "filename or extension is too long" error, especially on Windows | Passed a huge string as a CLI argument instead of via stdin | Pipe the payload to the tool's stdin instead of building one enormous command-line argument (e.g. `subprocess.run([...], input=big_string, ...)` rather than appending it to the argv list) |
| `spark.read.format("delta").load(path)` fails on a locally-built table (via `deltalake`/`delta-rs`) that reads back fine with `DeltaTable(path).to_pandas()` | Uploaded the Parquet data file(s) but not the entire `_delta_log/` folder (or vice versa), so Spark can't find a consistent commit log for the data present | Upload the *whole* local table folder tree, preserving relative paths — every file under `_delta_log/` and every `part-*.parquet`. See [delta-tables-without-spark.md](delta-tables-without-spark.md) |

## General debugging approach

1. Separate the two failure domains early: **Fabric REST API** problems (workspaces/items/jobs — wrong resource, wrong workspace, permissions) versus **OneLake file** problems (wrong URL shape, wrong token audience, missing files in a Delta tree). The error messages for both often look like generic 4xx/404s with little detail.
2. When something "looks empty" or "looks wrong" in a CDC-mirrored table, check the raw (pre-current-state) event history for that column before concluding the source system never populates it — see [cdc-mirroring-and-dedup.md](cdc-mirroring-and-dedup.md).
3. Re-verify with a fresh token before debugging further if more than ~45–60 minutes have passed since the last `az account get-access-token` call.
